title: PostgreSQL 18: Transaction Isolation
relevantSections: 13.2.1 Read Committed; concurrent row updates and search-condition re-evaluation
supports: The documented simple row-update case connects current-state conditional mutation to real database behavior. It does not identify the two teaching algorithms as PostgreSQL isolation levels or prove arbitrary multi-row invariants.

title: PostgreSQL 18: UPDATE
relevantSections: WHERE conditions; RETURNING; affected-row command count
supports: Conditional update and returned/affected-row evidence distinguish a mutation from no qualifying update. This supports a production discussion; the Java model executes no SQL.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Transactions
relevantSections: Grouping related changes; BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK
supports: Related database changes need a defined transaction boundary. Reservation acceptance and the separate atomicity publication/discard model illustrate original local rules; neither implements database durability or crash recovery.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Constraints
relevantSections: 5.5.1 CHECK constraints and restrictions involving other rows/tables
supports: A row check has a defined scope; a nonnegative inventory column alone does not establish the example's cross-record stock/allocation relationship. This existing source ID refers to the same pinned page used by data-access.

title: PostgreSQL 18: ROLLBACK
relevantSections: Description; discarding updates inside the current transaction
supports: A real SQL transaction discards its updates on rollback. The split teaching algorithm has no shared rollback boundary; its ABORT does not model PostgreSQL rollback failing. Staged discard supplies no crash-recovery guarantee.

title: PostgreSQL 18: COMMIT
supports: Real database COMMIT has a documented transaction publication and durability boundary. The original Java COMMITTED phase represents only local modeled publication, with no persistent recovery or acknowledgement protocol.
